sourceInformation.source: Pressure Cooker (Activision, 1983), designed by Garry Kitchen for Atari 2600
sourceInformation.tech: Three.js r180 (0.180.0), WebGPURenderer with WebGL2 compatibility, Rapier 3D 0.19.3, Gamepad API, Web Audio API, PeerJS 1.5.5, AI Hub Session Protocol v1 client 1.4.0; bundled with esbuild 0.25.12
sourceInformation.artDirection: Procedural cel-shaded geometry, ink silhouettes, warm mid-century diner palette, printed signs and checkerboard tiles
sourceInformation.animation: Three.js AnimationMixer, AnimationClip and keyframe tracks for chef scurry, breathing, squash, dispenser chug and wrapping; procedural steering and physics confetti
sourceInformation.audio: Original code-generated swing jingle, bass and percussion, synthesized kitchen effects and formant-filtered gibberish voices; music defaults to 10%; no audio files
sourceInformation.online: 1–4-player host-authoritative co-op through AI Hub; standalone PeerJS WebRTC rooms and same-origin BroadcastChannel rooms; 1–2 local co-op
sourceInformation.testing: 146-check headless suite: complete three-shift services on three seeds, keyboard, emulated standard gamepad, landscape and portrait touch, scoring, loss states, physics, procedural audio samples, two-page rooms, real WebRTC between isolated contexts, four AI Hub harness scenarios, WebGPU submission and GPU-loss recovery; 1920×1080 visual review. Physical controller, real mobile hardware and cross-network NAT traversal: unknown.
sourceInformation.research: Read Activision’s 1983 manual via AtariAge for catching, rejecting, recipe combinations, waves, eight difficulty/player variants, belt losses, rating and three chutes; inspected an Atari screenshot and descriptions of the oven, chef, bright colors and jingle; read Three.js r180 source, Rapier documentation, PeerJS documentation and AI Hub Session Protocol v1.

testingFeedback: 13 distinct issues were found by automated tests, screenshots and review, including input timing, controller room-code entry, floor visibility, world picking, departed seats, reused render IDs, event tags, GPU recovery cleanup, portrait framing, Hub timeout results, pre-round navigation and two test setup/counter problems. All were corrected.

Three could interrupt or prevent a service: unreliable keyboard handling, a departed same-device guest retaining a required order/seat, and a cleanup error after deliberate GPU loss. All were corrected.

The end-to-end keyboard sequence that places a topping, carries a burger and serves it; it exposed event timing bugs that the deterministic simulation tests could not. The AI Hub dedicated-server scenario also verified authority without a local player.
Reading instantaneous render statistics after taking a screenshot. Three.js resets those counters each animation frame; retaining the counters and waiting for GPU submission gave useful evidence.
engineFeedback: Three.js makes a custom cel-shaded kitchen and native keyframe animation straightforward, while WebGPURenderer also provides a WebGL2 compatibility path.

Headless Chromium needed --use-angle=swiftshader in addition to the supplied WebGPU flags. Three.js r180 also required releasing material and geometry listeners before retiring a lost renderer so recovery cleanup remained valid.
The entire kitchen simulation, order logic, controller navigation, accessible prompts, procedural audio and host-authoritative multiplayer.
Combining browser GPU initialization with physics, controller-first menus and replicated game state in a portable single file.
Provide a smaller built-in arcade UI and input layer with controller focus navigation.
promptFeedback: The specific 1983 reference, controller-first presentation, attract mode and complete-slice requirement gave the game a clear identity.

The standalone signaling service was unspecified, and SOURCE in the filename could mean the title alone or title plus year. I used embedded libraries, PeerJS signaling and the full source title and year.
Delivering a readable, complete kitchen game with offline packaging and both standalone and hub multiplayer in one HTML.
Specify a preferred standalone signaling service and desired session length, while retaining freedom over genre and interpretation.

aiHub.name: Press for Burgers
aiHub.description: Catch flying toppings, stack exact orders and hustle every burger to the right window. Work three increasingly hectic shifts alone or share the kitchen in four-player co-op.
aiHub.controls: Move: left stick / WASD / arrows; interact: Cross / E; reject: Circle / R; dash: Square / Shift; belt brake: R1 / Q; pause: Options / Esc; touch: drag and tap with assisted handling
